brewing.notes: A safe starting point for green tea: cooler water, short steeps, then adjust by taste.

description:
A specialty tea of Jing'an county in Jiangxi, grown mainly at Shuangxi village in Luowan township, in the Jiuling mountains. Despite the name baicha, meaning white tea, it is classed here with green teas.

Treat it as you would any green tea: cooler water, short steeps, and a seller who can say where and when it was picked.
history: It took five special prizes and a first prize at the eighth Zhongcha Cup national competition in 2009 and a gold award at the eighth international famous tea competition in 2010. The Jiangxi Tea Association named it among the province's ten famous teas in 2013. Little more is documented about its past.
processing: Typical of green tea: picked, heated soon after picking to stop oxidation, then shaped and dried.
harvest_season: Usually picked in spring, with the earliest pickings prized, as with most green teas.
appearance_dry: Tight, round, straight and even strands likened to phoenix feathers, frost-pale and glossy.
appearance_wet: Leaves open into whole clusters of jade white with green veins.
taste_profile: Fresh, rich aroma with a distinct note of licorice; sweet and gentle in the cup.
vintage_note: Green teas like this are normally sold as the current year's harvest and are best within a year of picking. It is not an ageing tea.
